```{r}
# ============================================================
# Locomotor activity analysis: Culex pipiens and
# Culex quinquefasciatus under long-day (LD) and short-day (SD)
# photoperiods
#
# Overview
#   This script processes TriKinetics locomotor activity monitor
#   recordings (one 32-channel monitor file per species x
#   photoperiod), builds average 24 h activity profiles, and tests
#   whether daily mean activity differs between species and
#   photoperiods.
#
# Workflow
#   1. Read each monitor file and keep the per-minute activity
#      counts ("Ct" rows) for all 32 channels.
#   2. Remove channels listed in EXCLUSIONS (see the settings
#      section below).
#   3. For each individual, average activity at each clock minute
#      over the first DAYS_USE complete calendar days of recording
#      (the window starts at the first midnight after recording
#      begins, so a partial first day is skipped).
#   4. Average these individual profiles to give a group profile
#      (mean +/- SEM) and smooth it with a centered circular moving
#      average (SMOOTH_WINDOW minutes, wrapping across midnight).
#   5. Screen for outlying individuals: (a) single-minute activity
#      above 5x the group median of individual maxima, and (b)
#      whole-day mean activity outside 1.5 x IQR of the group.
#      Flagged channels are reported; they are excluded only if
#      added to EXCLUSIONS.
#   6. Compute one daily mean activity value per individual and
#      compare groups with a two-way species x photoperiod model
#      (statistical approach below).
#
# Statistical approach (Step 10)
#   - Fit a linear model (species x photoperiod) and test residual
#     normality with the Shapiro-Wilk test (alpha = 0.05).
#   - Normal residuals: Type II ANOVA (car::Anova) with pairwise
#     contrasts from emmeans.
#   - Non-normal residuals and strictly positive response: refit on
#     the log scale; if those residuals are normal, use the
#     log-scale Type II ANOVA and contrasts.
#   - Otherwise: Aligned Rank Transform (ART) ANOVA with ART
#     contrasts (ARTool package).
#   - P-values are Holm-adjusted across all six pairwise
#     comparisons among the four species x photoperiod groups; the
#     two species-within-photoperiod comparisons are reported on
#     the box plot.
#
# Input
#   Four TriKinetics MonitorNN text files, named in CONDITIONS:
#   pipiens_LD.txt, quinque_LD.txt, pipiens_SD.txt, quinque_SD.txt.
#   Columns 2-3 hold the date and time, column 8 the data type
#   ("Ct" = counts), and columns 11-42 the 32 activity channels.
#
# Output (written to the working directory)
#   FigD_*_clockProfile_*.pdf/.png   24 h activity profile for each
#                                    species x photoperiod, plus a
#                                    combined four-panel figure
#   FigE_dailyMeanActivity_boxplot_*.pdf/.png
#                                    daily mean activity box plot
#                                    with significance brackets
#   activity_stats_full_results.txt  full statistical log
#   activity_stats_full_results.csv  the same results as tables
#
# Requirements
#   R with tidyverse, lubridate, readr, patchwork, car,
#   emmeans, ARTool and ggsignif.
#
# References
#   Wobbrock JO, Findlater L, Gergle D, Higgins JJ (2011). The
#     aligned rank transform for nonparametric factorial analyses
#     using only ANOVA procedures. Proc. ACM CHI 2011, 143-146.
#   Elkin LA, Kay M, Higgins JJ, Wobbrock JO (2021). An aligned
#     rank transform procedure for multifactor contrast tests.
#     Proc. ACM UIST 2021, 754-768.
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(readr)
library(patchwork)
library(car)
library(emmeans)
library(ARTool)
library(ggsignif)

# Start from a clean workspace.
rm(list = ls())

# ============================================================
# GLOBAL ANALYSIS SETTINGS
# ============================================================
DAYS_USE      <- 3     # number of complete calendar days analyzed per individual
SMOOTH_WINDOW <- 11    # width (in 1-min bins) of the moving-average filter

# ============================================================
# PLOT COLORS (Cx. pipiens, Cx. quinquefasciatus)
# ============================================================
COL_PIP  <- "#3B82B8"
COL_QUIN <- "#C65A1E"

# ============================================================
# SIGNIFICANCE LABELS (box plot)
# Size of the bold significance labels (asterisks / "ns") drawn
# above the brackets, in ggplot2 text-size units (size 5 is about
# 14 pt).
# ============================================================
SIG_LABEL_SIZE <- 5

# ============================================================
# NUMBER OF CHANNELS PER MONITOR (before any exclusions)
# ============================================================
EXPECTED_N_TOTAL <- 32

# ============================================================
# PHOTOPERIOD CONDITIONS
# Lights-on time (decimal hours), light-phase length (hours) and
# input files for each photoperiod.
#   LD = 15L:9D, lights on 06:03
#   SD =  9L:15D, lights on 08:00
# ============================================================
CONDITIONS <- list(
  LD = list(
    lights_on_h = 6 + 3/60,     # 06:03
    light_hours = 15,
    pip_path    = "pipiens_LD.txt",
    quin_path   = "quinque_LD.txt"
  ),
  SD = list(
    lights_on_h = 8.0,
    light_hours = 9,
    pip_path    = "pipiens_SD.txt",
    quin_path   = "quinque_SD.txt"
  )
)

# ============================================================
# CHANNEL EXCLUSIONS
# Channel numbers (1-32) removed from each species x photoperiod
# group before analysis; integer(0) means none are removed. The
# expected number of individuals per group is computed from
# EXPECTED_N_TOTAL minus the number of exclusions.
# ============================================================
EXCLUSIONS <- list(
  LD = list(
    pip  = c(8,15,16,26,27),
    quin = c(2,6,10,17,19)
  ),
  SD = list(
    # Channel 5: total activity 1655 vs. next highest 200 (8x the
    # group median); flagged as an outlier by the diagnostic.
    pip  = c(1,3,5,7,21),
    quin = integer(0)
  )
)

# ============================================================
# READ A TRIKINETICS MONITOR FILE
# Returns per-minute activity counts ("Ct" rows) for all channels
# (file columns 11-42) in long format: datetime, id (ch1-ch32),
# activity, species. Tab-delimited files are tried first, then
# whitespace-delimited.
# ============================================================
read_lam_monitorNN_Ct_32ch <- function(path, species_label, expected_n = 32) {
  df <- try(
    readr::read_tsv(
      path,
      col_names = FALSE,
      show_col_types = FALSE,
      progress = FALSE
    ),
    silent = TRUE
  )
  if (inherits(df, "try-error") || ncol(df) < 42) {
    df <- readr::read_table2(
      path,
      col_names = FALSE,
      progress = FALSE
    )
  }
  if (ncol(df) < 42) {
    stop("File has ", ncol(df), " columns; expected at least 42. File: ", path)
  }

  datetime <- suppressWarnings(parse_date_time(
    paste(df$X2, df$X3),
    orders = c(
      "d b y HMS",
      "d b Y HMS",
      "m/d/y HMS",
      "m/d/Y HMS",
      "Y-m-d HMS"
    ),
    tz = "UTC"
  ))
  if (sum(!is.na(datetime)) < 10) {
    stop("Datetime parsing failed for: ", path)
  }

  df_ct <- df %>%
    mutate(datetime = datetime) %>%
    filter(as.character(X8) == "Ct")
  if (nrow(df_ct) == 0) {
    stop("No 'Ct' rows detected in column 8 for: ", path)
  }

  tube_cols <- paste0("X", 11:42)
  out <- df_ct %>%
    select(datetime, all_of(tube_cols)) %>%
    mutate(across(-datetime, ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x)))) %>%
    rename_with(~ paste0("ch", seq_len(expected_n)), -datetime) %>%
    pivot_longer(-datetime, names_to = "id", values_to = "activity") %>%
    mutate(species = species_label) %>%
    filter(!is.na(datetime))

  n_ids <- n_distinct(out$id)
  if (n_ids != expected_n) {
    stop("Expected ", expected_n, " channels, but parsed ", n_ids, " in: ", path)
  }

  out
}

# ============================================================
# OUTLIER DIAGNOSTIC (single-minute activity)
# Within the analysis window, lists the highest single-minute
# counts and a per-individual summary, and flags individuals whose
# maximum single-minute count exceeds 5x the group median of
# individual maxima. Flagged individuals are reported only.
# ============================================================
diagnose_outliers <- function(df_long, prof_obj, species_name,
                               exclude_ids = character(),
                               top_n_minutes = 20) {
  one_min <- df_long %>%
    mutate(min_time = round_date(datetime, unit = "minute")) %>%
    group_by(id, min_time) %>%
    summarise(activity = sum(activity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  anchor   <- prof_obj$anchor
  end_time <- prof_obj$end_time

  df_window <- one_min %>%
    filter(min_time >= anchor, min_time < end_time) %>%
    filter(!id %in% exclude_ids) %>%
    mutate(clock_h = (hour(min_time) * 60 + minute(min_time)) / 60)

  cat("\n====================================\n")
  cat("OUTLIER DIAGNOSTIC:", species_name, "\n")
  cat("====================================\n")

  cat("\nTop", top_n_minutes, "highest single-minute activity values:\n")
  top_mins <- df_window %>%
    arrange(desc(activity)) %>%
    slice_head(n = top_n_minutes) %>%
    select(id, min_time, clock_h, activity)
  print(top_mins)

  cat("\nPer-individual summary (sorted by max single-minute activity):\n")
  per_ind_summ <- df_window %>%
    group_by(id) %>%
    summarise(
      total_activity = sum(activity, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_activity  = mean(activity, na.rm = TRUE),
      max_activity   = max(activity, na.rm = TRUE),
      max_clock_h    = clock_h[which.max(activity)],
      n_minutes      = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(max_activity))
  print(per_ind_summ, n = Inf)

  median_max <- median(per_ind_summ$max_activity, na.rm = TRUE)
  threshold  <- 5 * median_max
  flagged    <- per_ind_summ %>% filter(max_activity > threshold)

  cat("\nMedian individual max activity:", round(median_max, 3), "\n")
  cat("Flagging threshold (5x median max):", round(threshold, 3), "\n")

  if (nrow(flagged) > 0) {
    cat("\nFLAGGED individuals (likely outliers):\n")
    print(flagged)
  } else {
    cat("\nNo individuals flagged at 5x threshold.\n")
  }

  invisible(list(
    per_ind_summ = per_ind_summ,
    flagged      = flagged,
    threshold    = threshold
  ))
}

# ============================================================
# CIRCULAR MOVING-AVERAGE SMOOTHER
# Centered moving average over a 24 h profile of evenly spaced
# 1-min bins. The series wraps around midnight, so values near
# 00:00 and 24:00 are smoothed with data from both ends of the day.
# ============================================================
circular_moving_average <- function(x, window = 11) {
  if (window %% 2 == 0) stop("window must be odd for a centered moving average")
  half <- (window - 1) / 2
  n <- length(x)
  if (n < window) stop("Series shorter than the smoothing window.")

  x_padded <- c(utils::tail(x, half), x, utils::head(x, half))
  smoothed <- stats::filter(x_padded, rep(1 / window, window), sides = 2)
  as.numeric(smoothed[(half + 1):(half + n)])
}

# ============================================================
# 24 H ACTIVITY PROFILE
#   1) For each individual, average activity at each clock minute
#      over the first `days_use` complete calendar days.
#   2) Average the individual profiles to give the group mean and
#      SEM at each clock minute.
#   3) Smooth the group mean and SEM with a `smooth_window`-point
#      circular moving average.
# Returns the group profile ($summary), the individual profiles
# ($per_ind), the number of individuals and the analysis window.
# ============================================================
make_clock_profile_first_full_days_midnight <- function(df_long,
                                                        days_use = DAYS_USE,
                                                        expected_n_indiv = 32,
                                                        exclude_ids = character(),
                                                        smooth_window = SMOOTH_WINDOW) {
  if (length(exclude_ids) > 0) {
    df_long <- df_long %>% filter(!id %in% exclude_ids)
  }

  one_min <- df_long %>%
    mutate(min_time = round_date(datetime, unit = "minute")) %>%
    group_by(id, min_time) %>%
    summarise(activity = sum(activity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  file_start <- min(one_min$min_time, na.rm = TRUE)
  file_end   <- max(one_min$min_time, na.rm = TRUE)

  # The analysis window starts at the first midnight at or after
  # the start of recording, so a partial first day is skipped.
  anchor   <- ceiling_date(file_start, unit = "day")
  end_time <- anchor + days(days_use)

  if (end_time > file_end) {
    stop(
      "Requested ", days_use, " full days but the recording only spans from ",
      file_start, " to ", file_end, ". Reduce days_use or check the file."
    )
  }

  df_window <- one_min %>%
    filter(min_time >= anchor, min_time < end_time) %>%
    mutate(
      mod_min = hour(min_time) * 60L + minute(min_time),
      clock_h = mod_min / 60
    )

  if (nrow(df_window) == 0) {
    stop("No data in the midnight-anchored window. Check timestamps.")
  }

  n_indiv_window <- n_distinct(df_window$id)
  if (n_indiv_window != expected_n_indiv) {
    stop(
      "Expected ", expected_n_indiv,
      " individuals in the first ", days_use,
      " full days, but found ", n_indiv_window, "."
    )
  }

  # Step 1: each individual's mean activity at each clock minute,
  # averaged across the `days_use` days in the window
  per_ind <- df_window %>%
    group_by(id, mod_min, clock_h) %>%
    summarise(activity = mean(activity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  # Step 2: group mean and SEM across individuals
  summ <- per_ind %>%
    group_by(mod_min, clock_h) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_activity_raw = mean(activity, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_activity        = sd(activity, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_indiv            = n_distinct(id),
      sem_activity_raw    = sd_activity / sqrt(n_indiv),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(mod_min)

  n_bins <- nrow(summ)
  expected_bins <- 24 * 60
  if (n_bins != expected_bins) {
    warning(
      "Expected ", expected_bins, " one-minute clock bins but found ", n_bins,
      " - circular smoothing assumes an unbroken, evenly spaced 24h series. ",
      "Check for missing minutes before trusting the smoothed profile."
    )
  }

  # Step 3: smooth the group mean and SEM (circular, so there is no
  # discontinuity at midnight)
  summ <- summ %>%
    mutate(
      mean_activity = circular_moving_average(mean_activity_raw, window = smooth_window),
      sem_activity  = circular_moving_average(sem_activity_raw, window = smooth_window)
    )

  message(
    "Included channels: ",
    paste(sort(unique(per_ind$id)), collapse = ", ")
  )

  list(
    summary    = summ,
    per_ind    = per_ind,
    n_indiv    = n_distinct(per_ind$id),
    anchor     = anchor,
    file_start = file_start,
    file_end   = file_end,
    end_time   = end_time
  )
}

# ============================================================
# PLOT A 24 H ACTIVITY PROFILE
# Smoothed group mean (line) +/- SEM (ribbon), with the dark
# phase shaded grey. Unsmoothed values remain available in
# $summary as mean_activity_raw and sem_activity_raw.
# ============================================================
plot_clock_profile_with_dark <- function(summ_df,
                                         line_color,
                                         lights_on,
                                         lights_off,
                                         y_limits = NULL) {
  dark_df <- tibble(
    xmin = c(0, lights_off),
    xmax = c(lights_on, 24),
    ymin = -Inf,
    ymax = Inf
  )

  p <- ggplot(summ_df, aes(x = clock_h, y = mean_activity)) +
    geom_rect(
      data = dark_df,
      aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      fill  = "grey85",
      color = NA
    ) +
    geom_ribbon(
      aes(
        ymin = mean_activity - sem_activity,
        ymax = mean_activity + sem_activity
      ),
      fill  = line_color,
      alpha = 0.20
    ) +
    geom_line(color = line_color, linewidth = 1.1) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0, 24),
      breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 3),
      expand = c(0, 0)
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Time of day (h)",
      y = "Mean activity (counts / min)"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12)

  if (!is.null(y_limits)) {
    p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = y_limits)
  }

  p
}

# ============================================================
# MAIN LOOP
# For each photoperiod in CONDITIONS: read both species' files,
# build profiles, run the outlier diagnostic, and plot and save
# the activity profiles.
# ============================================================
results <- list()

for (cond_name in names(CONDITIONS)) {
  cond <- CONDITIONS[[cond_name]]
  excl <- EXCLUSIONS[[cond_name]]
  lights_off_h <- cond$lights_on_h + cond$light_hours

  if (!file.exists(cond$pip_path))  stop("Cannot find file: ", cond$pip_path)
  if (!file.exists(cond$quin_path)) stop("Cannot find file: ", cond$quin_path)

  # Convert excluded channel numbers to channel ids ("ch5") and
  # compute the expected number of individuals per group.
  exclude_pip_ids  <- paste0("ch", excl$pip)
  exclude_quin_ids <- paste0("ch", excl$quin)
  expected_n_pip   <- EXPECTED_N_TOTAL - length(excl$pip)
  expected_n_quin  <- EXPECTED_N_TOTAL - length(excl$quin)

  cat("\n############################################################\n")
  cat("# CONDITION:", cond_name, "\n")
  cat("############################################################\n")

  # ---- STEP 1: parse raw data ----
  pip_long <- read_lam_monitorNN_Ct_32ch(
    cond$pip_path, "Culex pipiens", expected_n = EXPECTED_N_TOTAL
  )
  quin_long <- read_lam_monitorNN_Ct_32ch(
    cond$quin_path, "Culex quinquefasciatus", expected_n = EXPECTED_N_TOTAL
  )

  # ---- STEP 2: build 24 h profiles ----
  pip_prof <- make_clock_profile_first_full_days_midnight(
    pip_long,
    days_use         = DAYS_USE,
    expected_n_indiv = expected_n_pip,
    exclude_ids      = exclude_pip_ids,
    smooth_window    = SMOOTH_WINDOW
  )
  message(
    cond_name, " PIP individuals used: ", pip_prof$n_indiv,
    " | excluded: ", if (length(excl$pip) == 0) "none" else paste(exclude_pip_ids, collapse = ", "),
    " | file start = ",       pip_prof$file_start,
    " | midnight anchor = ",  pip_prof$anchor,
    " | window end = ",       pip_prof$end_time
  )

  quin_prof <- make_clock_profile_first_full_days_midnight(
    quin_long,
    days_use         = DAYS_USE,
    expected_n_indiv = expected_n_quin,
    exclude_ids      = exclude_quin_ids,
    smooth_window    = SMOOTH_WINDOW
  )
  message(
    cond_name, " QUIN individuals used: ", quin_prof$n_indiv,
    " | excluded: ", if (length(excl$quin) == 0) "none" else paste(exclude_quin_ids, collapse = ", "),
    " | file start = ",        quin_prof$file_start,
    " | midnight anchor = ",   quin_prof$anchor,
    " | window end = ",        quin_prof$end_time
  )

  # ---- STEP 3: single-minute outlier diagnostic ----
  # Results are printed to the console; channels are excluded only
  # through EXCLUSIONS.
  pip_diag  <- diagnose_outliers(
    pip_long, pip_prof, paste0("Culex pipiens (", cond_name, ")"),
    exclude_ids = exclude_pip_ids
  )
  quin_diag <- diagnose_outliers(
    quin_long, quin_prof, paste0("Culex quinquefasciatus (", cond_name, ")"),
    exclude_ids = exclude_quin_ids
  )

  # ---- STEP 4: common y-axis for both species within a photoperiod ----
  global_y_max <- max(
    pip_prof$summary$mean_activity  + pip_prof$summary$sem_activity,
    quin_prof$summary$mean_activity + quin_prof$summary$sem_activity,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
  global_y_limits <- c(0, global_y_max * 1.05)

  # ---- STEP 5: plot profiles ----
  p_pip <- plot_clock_profile_with_dark(
    pip_prof$summary, COL_PIP,
    lights_on = cond$lights_on_h, lights_off = lights_off_h,
    y_limits = global_y_limits
  ) + ggtitle(
    bquote(italic("Cx. pipiens") ~ .(cond_name) ~ "(n =" ~ .(pip_prof$n_indiv) ~ ")")
  )

  p_quin <- plot_clock_profile_with_dark(
    quin_prof$summary, COL_QUIN,
    lights_on = cond$lights_on_h, lights_off = lights_off_h,
    y_limits = global_y_limits
  ) + ggtitle(
    bquote(italic("Cx. quinquefasciatus") ~ .(cond_name) ~ "(n =" ~ .(quin_prof$n_indiv) ~ ")")
  )

  # ---- STEP 6: save profiles ----
  pip_stub  <- paste0("FigD_Cxpip_clockProfile_first3FULLdays_midnight_", cond_name, "_smoothed_excl")
  quin_stub <- paste0("FigD_Cxquin_clockProfile_first3FULLdays_midnight_", cond_name, "_smoothed_excl")

  ggsave(paste0(pip_stub, ".pdf"),  p_pip,  width = 7, height = 3.6)
  ggsave(paste0(pip_stub, ".png"),  p_pip,  width = 7, height = 3.6, dpi = 600)
  ggsave(paste0(quin_stub, ".pdf"), p_quin, width = 7, height = 3.6)
  ggsave(paste0(quin_stub, ".png"), p_quin, width = 7, height = 3.6, dpi = 600)

  # ---- STEP 7: display profiles ----
  print(p_pip)
  print(p_quin)

  results[[cond_name]] <- list(
    pip_prof = pip_prof, quin_prof = quin_prof,
    pip_diag = pip_diag, quin_diag = quin_diag,
    p_pip = p_pip, p_quin = p_quin
  )
}

# ============================================================
# STEP 8: COMBINED PROFILE FIGURE
# Four-panel figure (patchwork): rows = photoperiod (LD, SD),
# columns = species.
# ============================================================
combined_plot <-
  (results$LD$p_pip | results$LD$p_quin) /
  (results$SD$p_pip | results$SD$p_quin)

print(combined_plot)

ggsave(
  "FigD_all_clockProfiles_first3FULLdays_midnight_smoothed_excl_combined.pdf",
  combined_plot, width = 12, height = 7
)
ggsave(
  "FigD_all_clockProfiles_first3FULLdays_midnight_smoothed_excl_combined.png",
  combined_plot, width = 12, height = 7, dpi = 600
)

# ============================================================
# STEP 9: DAILY MEAN ACTIVITY PER INDIVIDUAL
# ============================================================
# Each individual's 1440-minute profile (activity at each clock
# minute averaged over DAYS_USE days; $per_ind) is smoothed with
# the same circular moving average used for the group profiles
# and then averaged over all 1440 minutes, giving one daily mean
# activity value per individual. These values are used in the
# statistical analysis.
#
# A circular moving average with weights summing to 1 preserves
# the mean, so the smoothed and unsmoothed daily means are
# identical; both are computed and their maximum difference is
# printed as a check.
# ============================================================
subject_means <- bind_rows(lapply(names(results), function(cond_name) {
  r <- results[[cond_name]]
  bind_rows(
    r$pip_prof$per_ind %>%
      arrange(id, mod_min) %>%
      group_by(id) %>%
      summarise(
        daily_mean_activity_raw      = mean(activity, na.rm = TRUE),
        daily_mean_activity_smoothed = mean(circular_moving_average(activity, window = SMOOTH_WINDOW)),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(species = "pipiens", condition = cond_name),
    r$quin_prof$per_ind %>%
      arrange(id, mod_min) %>%
      group_by(id) %>%
      summarise(
        daily_mean_activity_raw      = mean(activity, na.rm = TRUE),
        daily_mean_activity_smoothed = mean(circular_moving_average(activity, window = SMOOTH_WINDOW)),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(species = "quinquefasciatus", condition = cond_name)
  )
}))
subject_means$group <- paste(subject_means$species, subject_means$condition, sep = " / ")
subject_means$group <- factor(
  subject_means$group,
  levels = c("pipiens / LD", "quinquefasciatus / LD", "pipiens / SD", "quinquefasciatus / SD")
)

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("CHECK: smoothed vs unsmoothed daily mean per individual (should match exactly)\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("Max |raw - smoothed| across all individuals:",
    max(abs(subject_means$daily_mean_activity_raw - subject_means$daily_mean_activity_smoothed)), "\n")

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("SUBJECT-LEVEL SMOOTHED DAILY MEAN ACTIVITY (one value per individual)\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
subject_summary <- subject_means %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(daily_mean_activity_smoothed),
            sd = sd(daily_mean_activity_smoothed), .groups = "drop")
print(subject_summary, n = Inf)

# ============================================================
# STEP 9b: WHOLE-DAY OUTLIER CHECK
# ============================================================
# Complements the single-minute diagnostic (Step 3) by flagging
# individuals whose daily mean activity lies outside
# Q1 - 1.5 x IQR or Q3 + 1.5 x IQR of their own group (the
# standard box-plot rule). Flagged individuals are reported only.
# ============================================================
flag_subject_outliers <- function(df, value_col, group_col = "group", id_col = "id") {
  df %>%
    group_by(.data[[group_col]]) %>%
    mutate(
      q1 = quantile(.data[[value_col]], 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
      q3 = quantile(.data[[value_col]], 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
      iqr = q3 - q1,
      lower = q1 - 1.5 * iqr,
      upper = q3 + 1.5 * iqr,
      is_outlier = .data[[value_col]] < lower | .data[[value_col]] > upper
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(is_outlier) %>%
    select(all_of(id_col), all_of(group_col), all_of(value_col), lower, upper)
}

subject_outliers <- flag_subject_outliers(subject_means, "daily_mean_activity_smoothed")

cat("\n---- Subject-level (whole-day) outliers, boxplot IQR rule ----\n")
if (nrow(subject_outliers) > 0) {
  cat("FLAGGED - these individuals' entire-day mean activity falls outside\n")
  cat("1.5x IQR of their own group, independent of any single-minute burst:\n")
  print(subject_outliers)
  cat(
    "\nIf these reflect real data-quality issues (e.g. a stuck/miscounting\n",
    "channel) rather than genuine biology, add their channel NUMBER to\n",
    "EXCLUSIONS[[condition]]$pip / $quin above and re-run the whole script -\n",
    "excluding them will also correctly update every profile/plot/stat that\n",
    "used that condition, not just this box plot.\n", sep = ""
  )
} else {
  cat("No subject-level whole-day outliers flagged.\n")
}

# ============================================================
# STEP 10: STATISTICAL ANALYSIS
# ============================================================
#   1) Two-way linear model (species x photoperiod); Shapiro-Wilk
#      test on residuals (alpha = 0.05).
#   2) Normal residuals: Type II ANOVA (car::Anova) and emmeans
#      pairwise contrasts among the four groups.
#   3) Non-normal residuals and strictly positive response: refit
#      on the log scale and retest; if normal, use the log-scale
#      Type II ANOVA and contrasts.
#   4) Otherwise: ART ANOVA (Wobbrock et al. 2011) with ART
#      contrasts (Elkin et al. 2021), ARTool package.
#   5) Holm adjustment across all six pairwise group comparisons,
#      after which the two species-within-photoperiod comparisons
#      are extracted for reporting.
# ============================================================

# ---- Split an emmeans/ART contrast label ("a b - c d") into its
#      two sides, each a vector of factor levels. ----

parse_contrast_sides <- function(contrast_str) {
  sides <- strsplit(contrast_str, " - ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  lapply(sides, function(s) strsplit(trimws(s), "[ ,]+")[[1]])
}

# ---- Keep only contrasts between species within the same
#      photoperiod. ----
extract_species_within_photoperiod <- function(contrast_df) {
  keep <- sapply(contrast_df$contrast, function(cs) {
    parts <- parse_contrast_sides(cs)
    if (length(parts) != 2 || any(lengths(parts) != 2)) return(FALSE)
    sp1 <- parts[[1]][1]; ph1 <- parts[[1]][2]
    sp2 <- parts[[2]][1]; ph2 <- parts[[2]][2]
    (ph1 == ph2) && (sp1 != sp2)
  })
  contrast_df[keep, , drop = FALSE]
}

# ---- Run the full analysis for one response variable and return
#      the model, normality results, ANOVA table and contrasts. ----
compare_groups_full_pipeline <- function(data, response, species_var = "species",
                                          photoperiod_var = "photoperiod", alpha = 0.05) {
  data <- as.data.frame(data)
  data[[species_var]] <- factor(data[[species_var]])
  data[[photoperiod_var]] <- factor(data[[photoperiod_var]])
  fml <- as.formula(paste(response, "~", species_var, "*", photoperiod_var))

  result <- list(response = response, alpha = alpha)

  m_raw <- lm(fml, data = data)
  sh_raw <- shapiro.test(residuals(m_raw))
  result$shapiro_raw_W <- unname(sh_raw$statistic)
  result$shapiro_raw_p <- sh_raw$p.value
  result$normal_raw <- sh_raw$p.value > alpha

  result$shapiro_log_W <- NA
  result$shapiro_log_p <- NA
  result$normal_log <- NA
  result$log_skipped_reason <- NA_character_

  scale_used <- NA
  model_used <- NULL

  if (sh_raw$p.value > alpha) {
    scale_used <- "raw"
    model_used <- m_raw
    result$decision_rationale <- sprintf(
      "Raw-scale residuals normal (Shapiro-Wilk W = %.3f, p = %.4f > alpha = %.2f); raw-scale Type II ANOVA used.",
      result$shapiro_raw_W, result$shapiro_raw_p, alpha
    )
  } else {
    all_positive <- all(data[[response]] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
    if (all_positive) {
      fml_log <- as.formula(paste0("log(", response, ") ~ ", species_var, " * ", photoperiod_var))
      m_log <- lm(fml_log, data = data)
      sh_log <- shapiro.test(residuals(m_log))
      result$shapiro_log_W <- unname(sh_log$statistic)
      result$shapiro_log_p <- sh_log$p.value
      result$normal_log <- sh_log$p.value > alpha
      if (sh_log$p.value > alpha) {
        scale_used <- "log"
        model_used <- m_log
        result$decision_rationale <- sprintf(
          "Raw-scale residuals non-normal (W = %.3f, p = %.4f); log-scale residuals normal (W = %.3f, p = %.4f > alpha = %.2f); log-scale Type II ANOVA used.",
          result$shapiro_raw_W, result$shapiro_raw_p, result$shapiro_log_W, result$shapiro_log_p, alpha
        )
      } else {
        result$decision_rationale <- sprintf(
          "Raw-scale residuals non-normal (W = %.3f, p = %.4f); log-scale residuals also non-normal (W = %.3f, p = %.4f); ART ANOVA used.",
          result$shapiro_raw_W, result$shapiro_raw_p, result$shapiro_log_W, result$shapiro_log_p
        )
      }
    } else {
      result$log_skipped_reason <- "response contains non-positive values"
      result$decision_rationale <- sprintf(
        "Raw-scale residuals non-normal (W = %.3f, p = %.4f); log transform not attempted (%s); ART ANOVA used.",
        result$shapiro_raw_W, result$shapiro_raw_p, result$log_skipped_reason
      )
    }
  }

  if (is.na(scale_used)) scale_used <- "ART"
  result$scale_used <- scale_used

  if (scale_used %in% c("raw", "log")) {
    result$model <- model_used
    result$anova_table <- car::Anova(model_used, type = 2)

    emm_fml <- as.formula(paste("~", species_var, "*", photoperiod_var))
    emm <- emmeans(model_used, emm_fml)
    full_contrasts <- as.data.frame(pairs(emm, adjust = "holm"))
    result$full_contrasts <- full_contrasts
    result$species_within_photoperiod <- extract_species_within_photoperiod(full_contrasts)
  } else {
    art_model <- art(fml, data = data)
    result$model <- art_model
    result$anova_table <- anova(art_model)

    art_term <- paste(species_var, photoperiod_var, sep = ":")
    full_contrasts <- as.data.frame(art.con(art_model, art_term, adjust = "holm"))
    result$full_contrasts <- full_contrasts
    result$species_within_photoperiod <- extract_species_within_photoperiod(full_contrasts)
  }

  # ---- One-row summary of the normality tests and the analysis
  #      used; rows from several response variables can be combined
  #      with rbind(). ----
  result$normality_path_row <- data.frame(
    outcome            = response,
    shapiro_W_raw       = round(result$shapiro_raw_W, 4),
    shapiro_p_raw       = round(result$shapiro_raw_p, 4),
    normal_raw          = result$normal_raw,
    shapiro_W_log       = if (is.na(result$shapiro_log_W)) NA else round(result$shapiro_log_W, 4),
    shapiro_p_log       = if (is.na(result$shapiro_log_p)) NA else round(result$shapiro_log_p, 4),
    normal_log          = result$normal_log,
    log_skipped_reason  = result$log_skipped_reason,
    scale_test_used     = c(raw = "Type II ANOVA (raw scale)",
                             log = "Type II ANOVA (log scale)",
                             ART = "Aligned Rank Transform ANOVA")[[scale_used]],
    decision_rationale  = result$decision_rationale,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  result
}

stats_result <- compare_groups_full_pipeline(
  subject_means, response = "daily_mean_activity_smoothed",
  species_var = "species", photoperiod_var = "condition"
)

cat("\n============================================================\n")
cat("STATISTICS PIPELINE RESULT\n")
cat("============================================================\n")
cat("\n---- Normality assessment and analysis path ----\n")
print(stats_result$normality_path_row)
cat("\n", stats_result$decision_rationale, "\n", sep = "")

cat("\n---- ANOVA (main effects + interaction) ----\n")
print(stats_result$anova_table)

cat("\n---- Full 6-comparison family, Holm-adjusted ----\n")
print(stats_result$full_contrasts)

cat("\n---- Species-within-photoperiod contrasts (for reporting) ----\n")
print(stats_result$species_within_photoperiod)

# ============================================================
# STEP 11: DAILY MEAN ACTIVITY BOX PLOT
# ============================================================
# One panel per photoperiod, each comparing the two species.
# Points are individuals (horizontally jittered for visibility).
# Brackets show the Holm-adjusted species-within-photoperiod
# comparisons from Step 10. Species names on the x-axis are
# italicized with plotmath italic() expressions.
box_data <- subject_means
species_label_text <- c("Cx. pipiens", "Cx. quinquefasciatus")
box_data$species_label <- factor(
  box_data$species,
  levels = c("pipiens", "quinquefasciatus"),
  labels = species_label_text
)
box_data$condition <- factor(box_data$condition, levels = c("LD", "SD"))

species_colors <- setNames(c(COL_PIP, COL_QUIN), species_label_text)

# Italic x-axis labels, matched to the factor levels by name.
species_axis_labels <- c(
  "Cx. pipiens"          = expression(italic("Cx. pipiens")),
  "Cx. quinquefasciatus" = expression(italic("Cx. quinquefasciatus"))
)

y_max <- max(box_data$daily_mean_activity_smoothed, na.rm = TRUE)
y_range <- diff(range(box_data$daily_mean_activity_smoothed, na.rm = TRUE))
bracket_y <- y_max + 0.08 * y_range

# Convert a p-value to a significance label.
stars_from_p <- function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("NA")
  if (p < 0.0001) "****"
  else if (p < 0.001) "***"
  else if (p < 0.01) "**"
  else if (p < 0.05) "*"
  else "ns"
}

swp <- stats_result$species_within_photoperiod
p_ld <- swp$p.value[grepl("LD", swp$contrast)][1]
p_sd <- swp$p.value[grepl("SD", swp$contrast)][1]

# One bracket per facet: ggsignif's manual mode draws each row into
# whichever panel matches its 'condition' value, since that column
# is also the faceting variable used below. The brackets are drawn
# without text; the significance labels are added as a separate bold
# text layer (sig_label_df) so their size and weight can be set.
sig_df <- data.frame(
  condition   = factor(c("LD", "SD"), levels = c("LD", "SD")),
  xmin        = c(1, 1),
  xmax        = c(2, 2),
  y_position  = c(bracket_y, bracket_y),
  annotations = c("", "")
)

sig_label_df <- data.frame(
  condition = factor(c("LD", "SD"), levels = c("LD", "SD")),
  x         = c(1.5, 1.5),
  y         = c(bracket_y, bracket_y) + 0.02 * y_range,
  label     = c(stars_from_p(p_ld), stars_from_p(p_sd))
)

p_box <- ggplot(box_data, aes(x = species_label, y = daily_mean_activity_smoothed, fill = species_label)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, alpha = 0.85, outlier.shape = 21) +
  geom_jitter(position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, seed = 42), alpha = 0.4, size = 1.2) +
  geom_signif(
    data = sig_df,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, y_position = y_position, annotations = annotations),
    manual = TRUE, tip_length = 0.02, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = sig_label_df,
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, fontface = "bold", size = SIG_LABEL_SIZE, vjust = 0
  ) +
  facet_grid(cols = vars(condition), scales = "free_x", space = "free", switch = "x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = species_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = species_axis_labels) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Daily mean activity (counts / min)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.placement  = "outside",
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey85", color = "grey30"),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1)
  )

print(p_box)

ggsave("FigE_dailyMeanActivity_boxplot_species_photoperiod.pdf", p_box, width = 6.5, height = 5.5)
ggsave("FigE_dailyMeanActivity_boxplot_species_photoperiod.png", p_box, width = 6.5, height = 5.5, dpi = 600)


# ============================================================
# STEP 12: SAVE STATISTICAL RESULTS
# ============================================================
# activity_stats_full_results.txt: text log of the results from
#   Steps 9-10 (group summaries, whole-day outliers, normality
#   tests and analysis path, ANOVA, all six contrasts, and the
#   species-within-photoperiod contrasts).
# activity_stats_full_results.csv: the same results as tables.
# ============================================================
stats_log <- capture.output({
  cat("============================================================\n")
  cat("SUBJECT-LEVEL SMOOTHED DAILY MEAN ACTIVITY (one value per individual)\n")
  cat("============================================================\n")
  print(subject_summary, n = Inf)

  cat("\n============================================================\n")
  cat("SUBJECT-LEVEL (WHOLE-DAY) OUTLIER CHECK - boxplot IQR rule\n")
  cat("============================================================\n")
  if (nrow(subject_outliers) > 0) print(subject_outliers) else cat("None flagged.\n")

  cat("\n============================================================\n")
  cat("NORMALITY ASSESSMENT AND ANALYSIS PATH\n")
  cat("============================================================\n")
  print(stats_result$normality_path_row)
  cat("\n", stats_result$decision_rationale, "\n", sep = "")

  cat("\n---- ANOVA (main effects + interaction) ----\n")
  print(stats_result$anova_table)

  cat("\n---- Full 6-comparison family, Holm-adjusted ----\n")
  print(stats_result$full_contrasts)

  cat("\n---- Species-within-photoperiod contrasts (for reporting) ----\n")
  print(stats_result$species_within_photoperiod)
})
writeLines(stats_log, "activity_stats_full_results.txt")

anova_df <- tryCatch(as.data.frame(stats_result$anova_table), error = function(e) NULL)

con <- file("activity_stats_full_results.csv", "w")
writeLines("SUBJECT-LEVEL SUMMARY", con)
write.csv(subject_summary, con, row.names = FALSE)
writeLines("", con)
writeLines("SUBJECT-LEVEL WHOLE-DAY OUTLIERS (boxplot IQR rule)", con)
if (nrow(subject_outliers) > 0) write.csv(subject_outliers, con, row.names = FALSE) else writeLines("None flagged", con)
writeLines("", con)
writeLines("NORMALITY ASSESSMENT AND ANALYSIS PATH", con)
write.csv(stats_result$normality_path_row, con, row.names = FALSE)
writeLines("", con)
writeLines("ANOVA (MAIN EFFECTS + INTERACTION)", con)
if (!is.null(anova_df)) write.csv(anova_df, con, row.names = TRUE) else writeLines("(see .txt log - object did not convert cleanly to a data frame)", con)
writeLines("", con)
writeLines("FULL 6-COMPARISON FAMILY, HOLM-ADJUSTED", con)
write.csv(stats_result$full_contrasts, con, row.names = FALSE)
writeLines("", con)
writeLines("SPECIES-WITHIN-PHOTOPERIOD CONTRASTS (FOR REPORTING)", con)
write.csv(stats_result$species_within_photoperiod, con, row.names = FALSE)
close(con)

message(
  "\nSaved complete statistical results to activity_stats_full_results.txt ",
  "and activity_stats_full_results.csv")
```
